mainTopic: The impure כהן's night routine, the morning lottery for תרומת הדשן, and the source for the כהנים guarding in three places
overview: The amud opens by finishing the משנה about a כהן who became impure during the night in the לשכת המוקד. He walks through a lit tunnel under the בית המקדש to the immersion room, which has a fire and a private bathroom. There he immerses, dries off and warms up, then waits with the other כהנים until the gates open and he leaves. The משנה then begins the morning service. Any כהן who wants to do תרומת הדשן must immerse before the ממונה arrives around קרות הגבר. The ממונה then runs a lottery among those who immersed. The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that the כהנים guard the בית המקדש in three places. אביי brings the פסוק about משה, אהרן and his sons camping east of the משכן. The גמרא reads that פסוק in two parts: משה stands for the לוים, while אהרן and his sons are the כהנים guarding in three separate places. רב אשי gives another source: the three 'guard' words at the end of the same פסוק.

steps.title: The impure priest's path to the immersion room
steps.stepSummary: The impure כהן walks through a lit tunnel under the בירה until he reaches the בית הטבילה, which has a fire and a בית הכסא של כבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He goes through a winding tunnel under the Temple building, with lamps lit on both sides, until he reaches the immersion room. There was a fire there and a respectable private bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is continuing its description of the כהן who became impure at night and is describing the route he takes to go immerse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he is impure, he cannot walk through the holy עזרה. So he goes under it through a tunnel. The room he reaches was set up for comfort and dignity, with a fire for warmth and a private bathroom.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple building and its grounds
The room with the מקוה for immersion
A fire, used to warm the כהנים

phrases.english: Through the winding passage that runs beneath the Temple building.
And lamps were burning on this side and on that side,
until he reaches the Chamber of Immersion.
And there was a fire there,
and a bathroom of honor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from before this section about the כהן who became impure at night.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The impure כהן reaches the immersion room by an underground lit tunnel. The room has a fire and a private bathroom.

steps.title: What made the bathroom honorable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the כבוד of the bathroom. A locked door meant someone was inside, and an open door meant it was empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was its honor: if he found it locked, he knew someone was inside. If it was open, it was clear that no one was inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the phrase it just used, 'bathroom of honor,' by describing the simple privacy system.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody had to knock or call out to find out whether the bathroom was taken. The door itself showed it, so the person inside kept his privacy and dignity.

keyTerms.meaning: Its honor, meaning the dignity it gave the user

phrases.english: This was its honor:

phrases.aramaic: מְצָאוֹ נָעוּל – יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם אָדָם.
phrases.english: If he found it locked, he knows that there is a person there.
If open, it is known that there is no person there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the term 'בית הכסא של כבוד' from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A locked door signals that the bathroom is occupied, and an open door signals that it is free. This keeps the user's privacy.

steps.title: Immersing, warming up, and waiting for the gates to open
steps.stepSummary: The כהן immerses, dries off, warms up by the fire, then sits with the other כהנים until the gates open, and then he leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went down and immersed, came up and dried off, and warmed himself by the fire. Then he came back and sat with his fellow כהנים until the gates were opened, and then he left.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the story of the impure כהן: how he purifies himself and what he does until morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After immersing he is still not fully pure until nightfall, so he cannot stay for the day's service. He waits with his brothers until the gates open in the morning and then leaves.
steps.whatToRemember: The impure כהן's night routine is: tunnel, immersion room, immerse, dry off, warm up, wait with the others, and leave when the gates open.

phrases.english: He went down and immersed,
came up and dried himself,
and warmed himself opposite the fire.

phrases.aramaic: בָּא, וְיָשַׁב לוֹ אֵצֶל אֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים,
phrases.english: He came and sat beside his brothers the priests,
until the gates were opened;
then he goes out and goes on his way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the impure כהן's routine after he reaches the immersion room.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The impure כהן immerses, warms up, waits with the other כהנים, and leaves once the gates open.

steps.title: Whoever wants to remove the ashes must immerse early
steps.stepSummary: A new section begins. A כהן who wants to do תרומת הדשן must get up early and immerse before the ממונה arrives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever wants to remove the ashes from the altar gets up early and immerses before the appointed officer comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now moves to the start of the morning service and gives the rule for who can join the first job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a כהן who has already immersed may join the lottery for תרומת הדשן. So anyone who wants a chance at this job must be ready before the ממונה shows up.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove the ashes from the altar (תרומת הדשן), the first service of the day
The appointed officer who runs the lotteries

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה לִתְרוֹם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: Whoever wants to remove the ashes from the altar,
rises early and immerses
before the appointed one arrives.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה לִתְרוֹם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the impure כהן's night to the start of the morning service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who wants to do תרומת הדשן must immerse before the ממונה arrives.

steps.title: When does the appointed officer arrive?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what time the ממונה comes, since the כהנים need to know how early to immerse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And at what time does the appointed officer come?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks itself a practical question, setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'immerse before the ממונה comes' only works if you know when he comes. So the משנה stops to ask about his timing.

phrases.english: And at what time does the appointed one come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the detail needed to apply the rule in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The time of the ממונה's arrival, which is the deadline for immersing.

steps.title: His arrival time varies around the rooster's call
steps.stepSummary: There is no fixed time. The ממונה comes at קרות הגבר, or close to it, either a little before or a little after.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not every time is the same. Sometimes he comes at the rooster's call, or close to it, either before or after.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question: the ממונה's arrival time is not fixed, but it is always around קרות הגבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he could come a little before the rooster's call, a כהן who wants the job cannot wait for the call. He has to be immersed even earlier to be safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Not all times are the same
The call of the rooster at dawn

phrases.english: Not all times are the same:
sometimes he comes at the call of the rooster,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ סָמוּךְ לוֹ מִלְּפָנָיו אוֹ מֵאַחֲרָיו.
phrases.english: or close to it, before it or after it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ממונה comes at קרות הגבר or slightly before or after it, so there is no fixed time.

steps.title: The officer knocks and runs the first lottery
steps.stepSummary: The ממונה knocks, the כהנים open for him, and he invites everyone who has immersed to join the פיס. The winner gets to do תרומת הדשן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The appointed officer came and knocked, and they opened for him. He said to them: 'Whoever has immersed, come join the lottery.' They held the lottery, and whoever won, won the job.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the actual moment the morning service begins, with the first lottery for removing the ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step shows why the rule in step 4 matters. Only those who already immersed are invited to the lottery, so a כהן who was late cannot compete for the job.
steps.whatToRemember: The day's service begins with a lottery run by the ממונה, and only כהנים who have already immersed may take part. The first lottery decides who does תרומת הדשן.

phrases.english: The appointed one came and knocked for them,
and they opened for him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: מִי שֶׁטָּבַל – יָבֹא וְיָפִיס,
phrases.english: He said to them: Whoever immersed, let him come and join the lottery.
They held the lottery; whoever won, won it.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the job of removing the ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what happens once the ממונה arrives, carrying out the rule from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only כהנים who have immersed join the lottery, and the winner performs תרומת הדשן.

steps.title: Where do we learn the כהנים' guard duty from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that the כהנים kept watch in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion by asking for the source in the תורה. This sets up the next step, where אביי will bring a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the כהנים kept watch in three places in the בית המקדש. The גמרא wants to know where the תורה teaches that this guarding is required.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? It asks for a source.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He's asking for the source of the משנה's rule that the כהנים stood guard in three places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins on the משנה's statement about the כהנים keeping watch.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה for the requirement that the כהנים keep watch in the בית המקדש.

steps.title: אביי brings the פסוק about guarding the משכן
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes the פסוק saying that משה, אהרן and his sons camped east of the משכן and kept its watch.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says, 'And those who camp in front of the משכן on the east, in front of the אהל מועד toward the sunrise, were משה, אהרן and his sons, keeping the watch of the מקדש, for the watch of בני ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a פסוק that talks about guarding the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the language of keeping a 'watch' (משמרת) over the מקדש. אביי takes this as the source that guarding is a real requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: the guarding or watch of the Sanctuary
those who camp, meaning those stationed there
the Tent of Meeting, which is the משכן

phrases.english: Abaye said: The verse states:
"And those that camp before the Tabernacle eastward,
before the Tent of Meeting toward the sunrise,
were Moses and Aaron and his sons,
keeping the watch of the Sanctuary,
for the watch of the children of Israel."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is במדבר 3:38, which speaks of keeping the watch of the מקדש.

steps.title: The פסוק puts כהנים and לוים together, but the משנה separates them
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק proves that guarding is required, but it does not match the משנה, which gives the כהנים three places and the לוים twenty-one separate places.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Yes, this shows in general that guarding is needed, and that כהנים and לוים guard. But the משנה teaches: 'The כהנים guard in three places in the בית המקדש, and the לוים in twenty-one places.' The פסוק, however, writes the כהנים and לוים together!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the פסוק teaches guarding in general. Then it challenges whether the פסוק fits the details of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was a לוי and אהרן was a כהן, so the פסוק shows that both groups guard. But it lists them all together in one spot, as if they guarded side by side. The משנה gives them separate places and separate numbers, so the פסוק seems to contradict it.

keyTerms.meaning: whereas; it sets up a contrast

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not rejecting אביי's פסוק. It agrees the פסוק proves guarding is needed. It only asks how the פסוק fits the משנה's separate places for כהנים and לוים.

phrases.english: They say: Yes,
we have found that a watch in general is required,
that priests and Levites keep watch.
But the mishna teaches:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת הַכֹּהֲנִים שׁוֹמְרִים בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: The priests keep watch in three places in the Temple,
phrases.notes: This is the first משנה of מסכת מדות.

phrases.english: and the Levites in twenty-one places,
whereas the verse,
writes priests and Levites together!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אִין, שִׁימּוּר בְּעָלְמָא אַשְׁכְּחַן דְּבָעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts אביי's source for guarding in general but challenges how well it fits the details of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's use of the פסוק as the source for the משנה's separate guard posts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק groups the כהנים and לוים together, while the משנה in מדות gives them separate places: three for the כהנים and twenty-one for the לוים.

steps.title: Read the פסוק in two parts: משה separately, then אהרן and his sons
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is split. 'Those who camp ... משה' refers to the לוים. 'Aaron and his sons keeping watch' refers to the כהנים: אהרן in one place and his sons in two.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said, this is what the פסוק means: 'Those who camp in front of the משכן on the east, in front of the אהל מועד toward the sunrise, are משה.' Then, separately: 'אהרן and his sons are the keepers of the watch of the מקדש.' אהרן guards in one place, and his sons in two places.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the פסוק as two separate statements, one about the לוים and one about the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With משה standing for the לוים, the כהנים are no longer grouped with them. The phrase 'אהרן and his sons' is then read as one post for אהרן and two posts for his sons. That adds up to exactly the three places in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it means; it introduces a new reading of the text

steps.whatToRemember: In this reading, משה stands for the לוים and 'אהרן and his sons' stands for the כהנים. אהרן's one post plus his sons' two posts give the three places of the משנה.

phrases.english: They say, this is what it is saying:
"And those that camp before the Tabernacle eastward,
before the Tent of Meeting toward the sunrise, were Moses,"
phrases.notes: The פסוק stops here for the first part. משה, who was a לוי, stands for the לוים' guard.

phrases.english: and then: "Aaron and his sons
are keepers of the watch of the Sanctuary."
Aaron, in one place,
and his sons, in two places.
phrases.notes: One plus two makes three, which matches the משנה's three places for the כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by rereading the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק by dividing it into two separate clauses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to put כהנים and לוים together in one guard post.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק has two parts: משה stands for the לוים, and 'אהרן and his sons' means the כהנים in three places (one plus two).

steps.title: How do we know to split the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the proof that the פסוק should be divided this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know the new reading is correct. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting the פסוק solved the problem, but it needs support from the wording of the פסוק itself. Otherwise it might look like a reading made up just to fit the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?

phrases.english: From where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of the split reading given in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis in the פסוק for dividing it into two separate groups.

steps.title: Two different words, two different groups
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק uses two different words, 'those who camp' and 'keeping watch.' This shows it is describing two separate groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written 'those who camp,' and it is also written 'keeping watch.' 'Camping' is one thing, and 'keeping watch' is another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its reading from the wording of the פסוק. The next step challenges how many places this gives the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone did the same job, the פסוק would not need two different words. 'Those who camp' goes with משה, meaning the לוים. 'Keeping watch' goes with אהרן and his sons, meaning the כהנים. So the two groups guard in separate places, just as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: from the fact that it is written

steps.whatToRemember: The two different words in the פסוק, חונים and שומרים, show two separate guard groups: the לוים and the כהנים. This alone does not yet prove three places for the כהנים. That is the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: From that it is written "and those that camp,"
and it is written "keeping watch."
"Those camping" are separate, and "those keeping watch" are separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 and backs up the reading given in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק uses two different words, חונים and שומרים, which shows two separate groups with separate guard posts.

steps.title: Maybe all the כהנים guard together in one place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading: even if 'אהרן and his sons' means the כהנים, maybe they all guard together in one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that all of them guard in one separate place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. Even if the end of the פסוק is about the כהנים, why should they have three posts instead of one shared post?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 showed that the כהנים are a separate group from the לוים. But being a separate group only proves they need their own place. It does not prove they need three places, which is what the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / maybe it means (used to suggest a different reading)

phrases.english: Say that all of them
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the כהנים, אהרן and his sons together.

phrases.english: guard in one separate place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the פסוק has two groups, then challenges the number of places for the כהנים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 11 that the כהנים guard in three places (אהרן in one, his sons in two).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק only shows that the כהנים are a separate group. That fits just as well with one shared post for all of them.

steps.title: Like משה, the כהנים each guard in their own separate place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea of one shared place. משה is listed in the same פסוק, and he was in his own place, so the כהנים are also not all grouped together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that. Just as משה was in one place by himself, so too אהרן and his sons were each in one place by themselves, not all together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It compares the כהנים to משה, who is mentioned right next to them in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה, אהרן and his sons are all listed together in one פסוק. Since משה clearly had his own separate spot, the פסוק is teaching that the people it lists are not lumped into one post. So the כהנים are split up and not all in one place.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't even think that (the suggestion is rejected)
Just as ... so too (a comparison that copies a rule from one case to another)

steps.whatToRemember: The comparison to משה shows that the כהנים in the פסוק do not all guard together in one post.

phrases.english: That should not enter your mind:
just as משה was in one place by himself,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו – בְּחַד מָקוֹם לְחוֹדֵיהּ.
phrases.english: so too אהרן and his sons were each in one place by themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison (מה ... אף) between משה and the כהנים, who are listed in the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All the כהנים might guard together in a single post.
steps.terutzMaskana: Just like משה, the כהנים are not grouped into one post. Each has a separate place, which supports the three places in the משנה.

steps.title: רב אשי learns the three places from the end of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different source for the three places of the כהנים: the end of the פסוק uses the word 'guard' three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: we learn it from the end of the פסוק, 'keeping the watch ... for the watch.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a different way to prove that the כהנים guard in three places. He points to the wording at the end of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the פסוק has three words from the root שמר, which means 'guard': שֹׁמְרִים, מִשְׁמֶרֶת and לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת. Three 'guard' words point to three separate guard posts. This way, רב אשי does not need the comparison to משה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the end of the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for the three places of the כהנים: the comparison to משה, or רב אשי's count of three 'guard' words at the end of the פסוק.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not disagree with the rule itself. Everyone agrees the כהנים have three places. He only gives a different source for it.

phrases.english: רב אשי said: from the end of the פסוק:
'keeping the watch ... for the watch.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 3:38. Count the words built on 'guard': there are three, and they stand for three guard posts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same rule that steps 11-15 proved through splitting the פסוק and comparing to משה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do we learn that the כהנים guard in three separate places?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the three 'guard' words at the end of the פסוק: שומרים, משמרת, למשמרת.
